key_insight: The paper introduces a filtering-based methodology that combines coarse-graining with volume penalization to quantify interscale energy transfer near solid boundaries, where standard Fourier or filtering diagnostics are insufficient.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical tool for analyzing boundary-layer energetics and wave–boundary interactions in geophysical and engineering flows with walls or immersed solids.
method: Combine coarse-graining with volume-penalization to preserve a physical representation of boundary effects.
Use the resulting filter to quantify linear energy transfer at solid boundaries.
Apply the framework to Rossby wave reflection to measure down-scale transfer at a western boundary.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an illustrative application to Rossby wave reflection off a western boundary, demonstrating the method on a bounded geophysical flow case.
watch_item: The approach is presented as a novel framework and its broader accuracy and robustness likely depend on careful implementation for different boundary geometries and flow regimes.
paper_title: A Methodology to Quantify Interscale Energy Transfer at Solid Boundaries
